user_input: I hate opening WhatsApp. Every single day another guy from my batch posts that 'pleased to share' screenshot on LinkedIn, and then our college group chat goes crazy with 'Congrats bro!' and 'Party kab hai?'. I’m sitting here with zero offers, a 7.2 CGPA, and three rejected technical rounds. I used to be happy for them, but now I just feel this sick, burning heat in my chest whenever I see their names. I’m starting to hate my friends just because they are succeeding and I’m rotting in my room.

My lab partner literally solved the entire DSA sheet during the summer break while I was struggling with depression and family drama. Now in labs, he writes optimal solutions in like five minutes and explains them to the professor while I’m still trying to debug a SegFault. He is so nice to me, which makes it even worse. I want to throw my laptop when he tries to help me because it just reminds me of how stupid and slow I am compared to him.

Sharma uncle's son got a 24 LPA package at Amazon, and now my dad won't stop bringing him up in every conversation. He keeps asking why I didn't apply for the same off-campus drive, even though he knows I was preparing for GATE. I literally feel this sick knot in my stomach every time my dad looks at his phone. I can't help but despise this guy I haven't even met in five years, just because his success is making my own parents look at me like I'm a massive financial failure.

They released the midterms stats today and the class average is 42/50. I got 31. This girl who sits behind me, who literally spends all day watching K-dramas, got a 48. I haven't slept more than 4 hours a night trying to pull my CGPA up, and she just glides through without even trying. I feel so much bitter resentment towards her that I couldn't even look in her direction during the tutorial today. Why does effort mean absolutely nothing in this stupid system?

My parents took a loan of 2 lakhs for this coaching institute, and I'm consistently scoring in the bottom 30% of the mock tests. Meanwhile, my roommate, who doesn't even have to worry about money and plays Valorant half the night, is in the top 5% every single week. I look at him sleeping peacefully while I'm shivering with panic at 3 AM, and I feel this toxic, dark hatred towards him. I hate that I envy his brain and his financial safety net so much it makes me physically sick.

My roommate just got an offer letter from Microsoft for 24 LPA. I am happy for him, I swear I am, but when he was celebrating on the phone with his parents, I had to lock myself in the common washroom so he wouldn't see me crying. I can't even clear the first round of basic DSA mock tests, and my CGPA is sitting at a miserable 6.8 with an active backlog in OS. Every time he talks about his prep or updates his LinkedIn, my chest gets so tight I feel like I'm going to throw up. How is everyone moving ahead so fast while I'm stuck in the exact same place?

My dad just called to ask why I didn't get shortlisted for the Amazon campus drive when 'Sharma ji's son' who is in my same batch got in. He literally said 'you both studied in the same coaching, what went wrong with you?'. I open our batch WhatsApp group and everyone is posting these green LeetCode streak screenshots and discussing their 4-star ratings on CodeChef. I have solved barely 50 easy questions and my head hurts every time I look at a DP problem. I hate that I'm starting to resent my friends for doing well, but their success feels like a direct spotlight on my failure.

They announced the 5th-semester CGPA sheets today on the notice board and my entire friend group is above 9.2, while I slipped to a 7.1. We went out for tea and they were all complaining about how 'hard' the grading was and how a 9.1 is going to ruin their profile, while I was literally trying to hide my face. I felt this sick, toxic wave of anger wash over me because their 'bad day' is a dream I can't even reach. I ended up making some stupid excuse and left early, and now I'm just sitting in my dark hostel room feeling so isolated and bitter.

My co-founder of our old college project just got selected for a fully funded research internship in Europe, and his LinkedIn is exploding with congratulatory messages from our professors. Meanwhile, my application for the same program got rejected in the first round, and I'm currently working a brain-dead, unpaid local internship just to keep my resume alive. I feel like an absolute fraud and a failure; we started at the exact same place, but he's flying to Munich and I'm stuck debugging legacy PHP code in a basement. I can't even bring myself to 'like' his post because the jealousy is eating me alive.

Every Sunday mock test is a nightmare because they publish the batch ranks publicly on the lobby wall. My bench partner always ranks in the top 10, and his parents are constantly sending him food and praise, while my mom only calls to ask why my rank fell by 50 spots. I look at him solving questions so effortlessly while I'm sweating over simple physics numericals, and I just feel this deep, hollow despair in my stomach. I've started skipping the post-test discussions altogether because hearing everyone talk about how 'easy' the paper was makes me want to disappear forever.

My roommate just bagged a 25 LPA package at a fintech firm during the day-1 placements, and I'm sitting here with my 7.2 CGPA and three pending DSA lab assignments, literally unable to breathe. We used to bunk classes together, but now his WhatsApp status is filled with congratulations, and my dad just called to ask why I wasn't shortlisted for the same coding round. I feel this sick, heavy knot in my stomach—I'm happy for him, but honestly, I mostly just hate myself and feel like a complete parasite who doesn't deserve to even be in this college.

Everyone in our batch discord is talking about their GSoc selections and open-source contributions while I couldn't even get my local Docker container to run for the Web-Dev project today. I used to be the 'smart kid' in school, but seeing my peers effortlessly post their internship offers makes me want to delete all my socials, smash my laptop, and just sleep for a year. I'm so angry at how easy it is for them, and then I feel incredibly guilty for being such an envious, bitter person.

My cousin and I are in the same branch, and he just cleared the first round of the MAANG interviews while I got rejected at the resume screening itself. Now my parents are lecturing me on how he spends 10 hours a day on LeetCode while I 'just waste time on my phone.' I literally can't face my family at dinner anymore, and seeing his LeetCode streak updates on LinkedIn makes me feel physically sick with envy and panic.

Sitting in the canteen listening to my project group talk about their off-campus offers feels like slow torture. I have two backlogs from my 3rd semester, my CGPA is stuck at 6.4, and hearing them discuss their 'lowball' 12 LPA offers makes me want to throw up because that amount would literally change my family's life. I feel so small and useless, like I'm playing a completely different, rigged game where I was destined to lose from day one.

We sit next to each other every day, but I feel like an absolute fraud who shouldn't even be allowed in the computer science department. I find myself hoping her code crashes during the demo just so I don't feel like the only incompetent idiot in the room, and that thought makes me feel like an incredibly toxic, horrible person.

My roommate just got his offer letter from Amazon today. 24 LPA. We used to study DSA together, but I got stuck on a simple backtracking question in the mock while he sailed through. I literally had to congratulate him with a fake smile while my stomach was twisting into knots. Why is it so easy for him while I'm drowning in backlogs and can't even clear the first round of basic coding assessments?

Every time I open LinkedIn, it's another 'thrilled to announce' post from classmates who didn't even know how to write a basic SQL query in sophomore year. Now they're securing high-paying roles at top startups, and here I am with a 6.8 CGPA, rejected from three mass-recruitment eligibility criteria before I could even sit for the aptitude tests. I feel this sick, burning hatred towards them, but honestly, I just hate myself for being this left behind.

I lost my temper and hung up on her, but now I’m just sitting in my hostel room crying because she's right to compare us. I'm struggling with the simplest dynamic programming problems in the lab while others are flying high, and I'm terrified I'll end up being the family disappointment.

I tried to sound excited on our group call, but I felt this toxic wave of envy wash over me because I'm stuck here clearing my math backlog in a tier-3 college. I'm starting to avoid his calls and mute the group chat because seeing his success just highlights how miserable and stuck my own life is.

My partner didn't even correct him or share the credit, just stood there soaking it all in. I feel so bitter and invisible because everyone thinks I rode on his coattails when I actually worked myself to exhaustion.

My mom called me an hour ago to ask if I'm even studying because 'Rahul’s parents are planning to buy a car with his sign-on bonus'. I feel this sick, hot lump of jealousy in my chest every time he talks on the phone with his parents, and then I hate myself for being such a horrible friend. My best friend got shortlisted for three different roles, and when he texted me to ask if I made it, I lied and said I didn't apply. I'm sitting in the dark in my hostel room, listening to people celebrate downstairs, feeling this horrible, toxic envy. I want to delete my account and disappear because I can't handle being the only left-behind loser.

My cousin just posted his 9.6 CGPA on the family group, and immediately my mom texted me asking why my grades are dropping. I'm struggling with a backlog in Microprocessors and can barely get out of bed, while he's getting research internships. I feel this intense, shameful hatred towards him every time my family brings him up. It's not his fault, but his success feels like a direct spotlight on my worthlessness, and I don't know how to stop comparing my messy life to his perfect run.

I literally can't look at LinkedIn or our batch WhatsApp group anymore. My lab partner just posted about bagging an internship at Microsoft with a 1.5L stipend, and my hands started shaking. I'm struggling to even compile my basic DSA trees code for tomorrow's lab, and my CGPA is a pathetic 6.8. I feel this sick, heavy knot in my stomach because we used to study together, and now I just hate him. Why does his success make me feel like I should just stop existing?

My roommate got placed in a Tier-1 firm today while I got rejected in the technical round because of a stupid edge case. Tonight his parents called him and they were crying of joy over speakerphone—I could hear it through the wall. My own dad keeps forwarding me articles about high packages and asking when my company results will come. I feel so incredibly bitter and small, sitting here pretending to be happy for him while feeling like an absolute failure.

I saw the grading sheet for the DBMS project and my best friend topped the class. I got a 'C' because I had a panic attack during the viva and couldn't explain normalization properly. I've been avoiding her texts all day because every time I see her typing, I feel this toxic wave of resentment. She has a loving family, a 9.2 CGPA, and everything is so easy for her, while I have to fight my own brain just to get out of bed.

Everyone in my department is talking about their winter internships and research papers, and I have absolutely nothing to show for myself. I spend my nights endlessly scrolling through their profiles, watching them get funded or win hackathons while I struggle with backlog exams. I feel like this parasitic impostor who somehow slipped into this college but doesn't actually belong here. I just want to disappear so I don't have to face them in the labs tomorrow.

My cousin who is the same age as me just got a 24 LPA package, and my relatives have been calling my mom to congratulate her while subtly rubbing it in. My mom is so depressed she won't even talk to me properly, and I can feel her silent disappointment every time I walk past her room. I'm preparing for mass recruiter exams next week and the salary is barely a fraction of that. I feel this intense, poisonous rage towards my cousin for existing and ruining my relationship with my mother.

My roommate just cracked a 25 LPA offer at Amazon and everyone in our hostel wing is celebrating in his room. I’m sitting here staring at my red Leetcode submissions, feeling this absolute sick feeling in my stomach because I couldn't even clear the first round of the same company. I want to be happy for him, he's my friend, but honestly, I just feel this burning wave of disgust at myself and a weird anger toward him that I can't shake off. My parents just called asking if I heard about his placement and why I haven't gotten any callbacks yet. I feel like such a massive failure.

Every time the class group-chat pings with exam sheets and CGPA updates, I feel like throwing up. My lab partner got a 9.4 CGPA and immediately posted it on LinkedIn with that annoying 'humbled and honored' template, while I’m barely scraping a 6.8 with two backlogs to clear. I’ve muted all notifications but the envy is literally eating me alive from the inside out. I used to be the smart kid in school, and now I'm just the mediocre background noise in everyone else's success story.

I can't even look at my desk partner anymore. We started learning web dev together, but he already bagged a high-paying remote internship while I'm still struggling with basic React hooks and failing midterms. I find myself hoping he messes up his project or gets scolded by the senior dev, and then I feel utterly sickened by my own toxic thoughts. What kind of terrible person envies their own friend this much? I feel so dirty and lonely.

My dad just sent me a screenshot of our neighbor’s son’s LinkedIn update about getting into an elite product-based company. He added a single text: 'He didn't even have a coaching loan, look at him.' I have worked 14-hour days trying to clear my DSA backlogs, but seeing everyone else pass me by makes me want to drop out entirely. Why does it feel like everyone else got the instruction manual for life while I'm just fumbling in the dark?

During today's project evaluation, the professor praised my group mate’s system design for ten straight minutes while barely acknowledging my contribution to the database architecture. My group mate just smirked and took all the credit without mentioning we did it together. I am sitting in the library now, too angry to cry, watching him talk animatedly to a group of girls about his upcoming interview. I hate how easy everything is for him, and I hate myself for being so completely invisible.

My roommate just got an offer from Amazon for a summer SDE role, and I'm sitting here struggling with basic DP questions in our DSA lab. Every time he types on his mechanical keyboard, it feels like a countdown to my failure. We literally have the same CGPA, we studied the same sheets, but he just got it easily. I feel this sick, burning knot in my stomach every time he talks to his parents about his CTC, and then my dad calls asking why I haven't cracked a single mock interview yet. I hate how much I resent him because he's actually a nice guy, but seeing his success is making me want to throw up.

Just saw the placement cell excel sheet update on our WhatsApp group. My batchmate who literally copied my DBMS assignments last semester got a 14 LPA package, and I got rejected in the first round of the same company. I can't stop staring at the spreadsheet. It feels so unfair, like I'm doing everything right—grinding LeetCode, keeping my CGPA at 8.7, fixing my resume—but the universe is just rewarding the ones who cheat the system. My chest is so tight right now, and I can't even face my parents when they ask about my shortlists tonight.

My childhood best friend and I joined the same B-tech college, but now she’s in the elite coding club and got a high-paying internship, while I’m stuck with two backlogs in math. She keeps trying to hang out and buy me coffee to 'celebrate,' but every time she speaks, I just feel this toxic wave of bitterness. I literally lied and told her I had a family emergency just to avoid seeing her success in person. I feel like an absolute monster for hating her growth, but her life is moving at hyperspeed while I'm drowning in basic math concepts.

I had to mute our college group chat because everyone is posting their LinkedIn updates. Every single notification feels like a personal slap in the face. I failed my system design interview yesterday, and seeing people who barely knew how to compile a C++ program last year get into top-tier tech firms makes me feel so small. I'm locked in my hostel room, eating cold maggi, wondering why my brain is so slow compared to everyone else's. My parents worked so hard to pay my fees, and I'm just here rotting while my peers thrive.

We got our midterm papers back for the operating systems lab today. The guy next to me got 28/30 and started whining about how he 'ruined his perfect GPA,' while I got 14/30 and barely passed. I wanted to scream at him or rip his paper up. I worked so hard, pulled three all-nighters, but his effortless intelligence makes all my sacrifices look like a joke. Now I'm sitting in the library bathroom stalls trying to stop my hands from shaking before my next class, feeling incredibly bitter and stupid.

My roommate just got placed at a fintech firm with a 24 LPA package. I've been grinding DSA for months, but I got rejected in the first round of the same company. My dad called me today and spent 15 minutes asking why I couldn't crack it when my roommate did, saying 'he studies in the same room, right?' I feel this sick, burning knot in my stomach every time I look at him now. I want to be happy for him, but honestly, I just feel like throwing up and hiding under my bed.

Everyone in our WhatsApp group is sharing screenshots of their 9+ CGPA this semester. I barely scraped a 7.2 because of my backlogs, even though I pulled all-nighters for every single midterm. My lab partner, who literally copied my system design code, got an S grade because she aced the viva. I can’t stop scrolling through LinkedIn seeing everyone land remote internships. I hate how bitter I’ve become, but seeing them succeed makes me feel like I'm completely invisible and failing at life.

I messed up my LeetCode contest again, couldn't even solve the second medium question. Meanwhile, this guy in my branch who started coding just 3 months ago is already talking about his Div 2 ranking and mocking people who struggle with dynamic programming. I felt so angry and small during the DSA lab today that my hands were shaking. I used to love tech, but now I feel like an absolute fraud who shouldn't even be in this engineering college.

During the mock GD today, my close friends were so articulate and confident, speaking about systems architecture like it's nothing. I sat there frozen, my mind completely blank, stuttering when the moderator finally called my name. Afterwards, they were all laughing and planning to apply for this premium product-based startup, and I had to make an excuse to go to the washroom just so they wouldn't see me cry. I feel so much envy toward their ease and charm, and it makes me feel like a horrible, toxic friend.

My cousin just got a massive referral at a MAANG company, and my mom won't stop talking about it on the family group. I'm currently struggling with my final year project, my guide is constantly rejecting my drafts, and I don't even have a single job offer in hand. Every time my mom mentions him, I feel this intense wave of anger and resentment towards him, even though he's done nothing wrong to me. I hate my life, I hate that I'm this petty, and I'm terrified I'll end up unemployed while everyone else moves ahead.

My roommate just got a 45 LPA offer from a top fintech firm while I’m sitting here struggling to compile a simple BFS graph traversal in our DSA lab. Every time he gets a notification on his phone, my chest tightens and I feel this sick, hot surge of anger in my throat, even though he's my friend. My parents keep asking when I’ll land a similar package because they took out a loan for my fees, and I feel like an absolute fraud who shouldn't even be in this college.

I can't even open LinkedIn or WhatsApp anymore. Everyone is posting these fancy certificates, GSoC selections, and 'thrilled to announce' internship updates while my CGPA just dropped to 6.8 after midterms. I feel like I'm sinking in quicksand while my batchmates are building rockets, and this ugly jealousy is eating me alive from the inside out.

My best friend since high school just cleared the Google L3 coding round, and instead of being happy, I spent the entire night crying in the common room bathroom. We used to fail chemistry together, and now she is on her way to a dream life while I have two active backlogs and can barely get out of bed to attend lectures. I hate myself for being this bitter, but I feel so left behind and worthless.

During today's project evaluation, the prof praised my lab partner's system design architecture for ten minutes straight while barely even acknowledging my contribution. He’s already got three research papers and I can't even sleep because my heart runs a marathon every time I think about placement season next month. I find myself wishing he would fail just so I can feel equal to him, and that thought makes me feel like a horrible, toxic person.

Every family dinner is just my dad talking about how our neighbor's son got placed in a US-based remote startup with a signing bonus, while I couldn't even clear the first round of TCS Ninja. I see my friends sharing memes about failing exams on the group chat, but then I find out they're secretly studying 10 hours a day and landing dream offers. I feel so betrayed and stupid for trusting their casual attitude while I actually fell behind.

My roommate just got a 45 LPA offer at a high-frequency trading firm, and here I am, still struggling to debug a simple DFS tree in my DSA mock run. He doesn't even study that much, he just sits there playing Valorant while I sweat over LeetCode medium questions all night. Everyone on our hostel WhatsApp group is reacting with fire emojis to his placement news. I literally had to lock myself in the washroom because my hands started shaking and I felt this sick, burning knot in my stomach. I feel so incredibly small and stupid next to him, like what is the point of even trying anymore?

Just saw my cousin's LinkedIn update about landing an internship at Google. My dad immediately sent the screenshot to our family group chat with no caption, just a silent, heavy guilt-trip. I have three active backlogs in my core ECE subjects and my CGPA is a literal joke at 6.2. I've spent the last two days staring at my IDE, unable to write a single line of code because my head is spinning with how my cousin is going to get a fat package and I'll end up in some mass-recruiter basement. I hate how much I resent him right now, he's a nice guy but his success feels like a direct verdict on my failure.

My lab partner got selected for the fully-funded summer research program in Germany, the exact one I spent three months drafting proposals for. When she told me, I had to fake this high-pitched, fake-happy voice to congratulate her, but inside I wanted to throw up. I've been pulling all-nighters for our DBMS project while she barely did any heavy lifting, but the prof loves her because she's extroverted. I'm sitting in the library right now, fighting back tears because my hard work feels invisible and her luck feels like a personal insult to my effort.

During our mock viva today, the external evaluator praised my closest friend's system design diagram for ten whole minutes, while he basically tore mine to shreds in front of the whole batch. This friend and I started coding together from first semester, but now he is talking about system design, microservices, and load balancers while I'm still trying to wrap my head around basic OS concepts. He tries to help me but his pity hurts even more than the evaluator's insults. I feel this awful, cold distance growing between us because I can't stand looking at how far ahead he has run.

The class topper just posted her placement package details on her Instagram story with some cheesy 'hard work pays off' caption. I failed the technical round of that same company last week because of a stupid runtime error on a graph problem I actually knew how to solve. I can't stop checking her social media and comparing our resumes, and every time I do, my chest gets so tight I can't breathe properly. It feels like she got the life I was supposed to have, and I'm left behind in the dust with nothing but a mountain of coaching loans and a rejection email.
